evidence.name: Prediction space and model image M = Y(Θ) ⊆ P
evidence.equation: P = ℝᵐ with metric Σ⁻¹ (m outputs), or a function space with a stated inner product. M = Y(Θ) ⊆ P is the model image (a set); it is a smooth model manifold only on a regular region (constant local rank, locally injective). Rank loss, non-identifiability, self-intersections, singular strata and boundary strata can occur (MMPa, MMPb, MMPj). Example: for the specific model e^{−θ₁T} + e^{−θ₂T} in L²(0, ∞) the Fisher metric is g_ij = 2/(θᵢ + θⱼ)³ (not a general formula, MMPk); dim P = ∞ while dim M = 2

evidence.name: Model rule and parameter domain fix the allowable model image
evidence.equation: the model rule Y and the domain Θ fix the model image M = Y(Θ). θ ∈ Θ is a parameter value and Y(θ) its prediction; parameters parameterize the image and give local coordinates only where the parameterization is locally regular and locally identifiable; different θ may give the same prediction (MMPb). Parameter limits can produce limiting strata of the image; ∂Θ, parameter limits, their images, MBAM strata and the topological boundary of Y(Θ) are different objects (MMPi, MMPj)

Under an invertible reparametrization (R1): rank, nullity, null directions, lengths, the full volume element √det g_θ dθ¹⋯dθⁿ, curvature and image-defined quantities are invariant; entries, det g, √det g alone, raw Fisher and Hessian eigenvalues, the condition number, J_Y singular values and chart-defined widths are not (MMIb, MMIc, MMPf–MMPh). For a change between fixed positive-definite weights the null directions and rank do not change; a singular weight or a θ-dependent noise law can change them (MMPd, MMPe). Geometric widths defined from the image are CONDITIONAL until their source definitions are fixed (MMPg)
